questions.question: Three pipes L, M and N can fill a tank in 10, 20 and 30 hours respectively. If L is open all the time and M and N are open for one hour each alternately, then the tank will be full in?
questions.explanation:
Calculations:

(L+M)’s 1 hour’s work = \(\left( \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{20} \right) = \frac{3}{20}\)
(L +N)’s 1 hour’s work = \(\left( \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{30} \right) = \frac{2}{15}\)
Part filled in 2 hrs. = \(\left( \frac{3}{20} + \frac{2}{15} \right) = \frac{17}{60}\)
Part filled in 6 hrs. = \(\left( 3 \times \frac{17}{60} \right) = \frac{17}{20}\)
Remaining Part = \(\left( 1 - \frac{17}{20} \right) = \frac{3}{20}\)
Now, it is the turn of L and M, and \(\frac{3}{20}\) part is filled by L and M in 1 hour.
Therefore, the Total time taken to fill the tank = (6+1) hrs. = 7 hrs.

Alternate Solution:

LCM of 10, 20, and 30 is 60.

Pipes   Efficiency
L = 10   6
M = 20 60 3
N = 30   2

According to Qn,

L is open all the time, and M and N are open for one hour each alternately, then the tank will be full in,

= (6 + 3) + (6 + 2) + (6 + 3) + (6 + 2) + (6 + 3) + (6 + 2) + (6 + 3)

= 9 + 8 + 9 + 8 + 9 + 8 + 9

= 60

1st hour: L + M → 6 + 3 = 9
2nd hour: L + N → 6 + 2 = 8
3rd hour: L + M → 9 units
4th hour: L + N → 8 units
5th hour : L → 9 units

6th hour: 8

7th hour: 8

Total 7 hrs required.

questions.question: A tank is 35 full. If 26 liters of water is added to the tank, it becomes 89 full. The capacity of the tank is:
questions.explanation:
Let the quantity of the tank be 5x l.

Tank full \(= \ \frac{3}{5} \times 5x = 3x\ l\)

When, 26 l of water is added;

\(3x + 26 = \ \frac{8}{9} \times 5x\ \)

\(= > 3x + 26 = \frac{40x}{9}\)

\(= > 26 = \frac{13x}{9}\)

\(= > x\  = 18\ l\)

Therefore; total quantity \(= \ 5x = \ 90\ l\)

questions.question: If pipe A and B working together can fill a tank in 6 hours, and pipe A can fill the tank 5 hours faster than pipe B, then in how much time pipe B alone can fill the tank?
questions.explanation:
When two pipes can fill the tanks individually in x and y hours then together they can fill the tank in \(\frac{\text{xy}}{x + y}\)

Given:

Pipe A and B can fill the tank = 6 hours

Formula

Work done = Time × Efficiency

Let pipe B can fill the tank in x hours

Pipe A will take = x - 5 hours

Now

\(\frac{1}{x}\) + \(\frac{1}{x - 5}\) = \(\frac{1}{6}\)

⇒ 6(x - 5 + x) = x2 - 5x

⇒ 12x - 30 = x2 - 5x

⇒ x2 - 17x + 30 = 0

⇒ x2 - 15x - 2x + 30 = 0

⇒ x(x - 15) - 2(x - 15) = 0

⇒ (x -15)(x - 2) = 0

x = 15 and x = 2

If x = 2, A = - 3 and time cannot be negative

So x = 15 hours

∴ B will fill the tank in 15 hours.

questions.question: A large Water tank can be filled by two pipes M and N in 60 minutes and 40 minutes respectively. How many minutes will it take to fill the tanker from empty state if N is used for half the time and M and N fill it together for the other half?
questions.explanation:
Part filled by (M + N) in 1 minute = \(\left( \frac{1}{60} + \frac{1}{40} \right) = \frac{1}{24}\)

Suppose the water tank is filled in x minutes.

Then, \(\frac{x}{2}\left( \frac{1}{24} + \frac{1}{40} \right) = 1\)

\(\frac{x}{2} \times \frac{1}{15} = 1\)

x = 30 min.

questions.question: To fill a cistern, pipes X, Y and Z take 10 minutes, 30 minutes and 15 minutes respectively. What is the time that the three pipes together will take to fill the cistern?
questions.explanation:
Calculations:

X can do a piece of work in 10 minutes.

Y can do a piece of work in 30 minutes.

Z can do a piece of work in 15 minutes.

Minutes' work of all three pipes together = 110+ 130+ 115 = 630= 15part

To fill the whole cistern, time taken = 115 = 5 minutes

Alternate Solution:

LCM of 10, 30, and 15 is 30. 

Pipes   Efficiency
X = 10   3
Y = 30 30 1
Z = 15   2

Total time required = 303+1+2 = 306 = 5 minutes.

questions.question: Two pipes P and Q can fill a tank in 60 hours and 15 hours respectively. If both the pipes are opened in a one-fourth filled tank, then in how much time 3/4th of the tank will be filled?
questions.explanation:
Let the capacity of the tank = 60 liters (LCM of 60 and 15) and the required time = t hours, then

Efficiency of pipe P  6060= 1 Litres/hr

Efficiency of pipe Q  6015 = 4 Litres/hr

3/4 th of the tank, 

34×60=45

Time taken by P and Q filled 45 L tank

t=45(4+1)=9

Hence, the answer is 9 hours.

questions.question: Pipe 'A' can fill a tank in 12 hours while pipe ' \(B\) ' empties it in 10 hours. When the tank was empty, pipe 'A' was opened and after 8 hours pipe ' \(B\) ' is also opened. In how much time will the tank get empty, again?
questions.explanation:
Let the total capacity of the tank be 60 units
Efficiency of pipe ' \(A\) ' \(=\frac{60}{12}=5\) units/hour
Efficiency of pipe 'B' \(=\frac{60}{10}=6\) units/hour
Tank filled in 8 hours \(=8 \times 5=40\) hours
Required time taken to empty the tank, again \(=\frac{40}{6-5}=40\) hours
Hence, option b.

questions.question: Two pipes J and K can fill a tank in 20 hours and 30 hours respectively. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, find after how much time should pipe K be closed so that the tank is full in 18 hours?
questions.explanation:
Let the capacity of the tank be LCM (20, 30) = 60 units
Efficiency of pipe J = 6020 = 3 units/hour
Efficiency of pipe K = 6030 = 2 units/hour
The combined efficiency of pipes J and K = 5 units/hour
Let both J and K be opened for ‘n’ hours and then, K be closed and only J be opened for the remaining

’18 – n’ hours.
5n + 3 × (18 – n) = 60
2n + 54 = 60
2n = 6
n = 3 hours

Alternate Method:

Pipe J fills tank in 20 hours
Pipe K fills tank in 30 hours
Both opened together,
The tank must be completely filled in 18 hours
We need to find after how many hours K should be closed.
Take LCM of 20 and 30 = 60 units (total tank capacity = 60 units)
Work done per hour 
J = 60 ÷ 20 = 3 units/hour
K = 60 ÷ 30 = 2 units/hour
Let pipe K be open for x hours.
So, J will be open for 18 hours (full duration).
Total work =
(J’s 18 hours work) + (K’s x hours work) = 60 units
3×18 + 2×x = 60
54 + 2x = 60
2x = 6
x = 3 hours
Pipe K should be closed after 3 hours so that the tank is full in 18 hours.

questions.question: A, B and C can fill a tank in 6 hours. When the three worked together for 2 hours, C was closed and A and B filled the remaining tank in 7 hours. How many hours would it take C alone to fill the tank?
questions.explanation:
Part of the tank which was filled in 2 hours \(= \frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}\)

The part of the tank remaining to be filled \(= \ 1\ –\ \frac{1}{3}\  = \frac{2}{3}\ \)

Work done by A and B together in 7 hours = \(\frac{2}{3}\)

Work done by A and B together in 1 hour = \(\frac{2}{3 \times 7} = \frac{2}{21}\ \)

Work done by C in 1 hour = [{(A+B+C)’s 1 hour’s work} – {(A+B)’s 1 hour’s work}]

\(= \ \left( \frac{1}{6} \right)–\ \left( \frac{2}{21} \right) = \frac{1}{14}\)

C alone takes 14 hours to fill in the tank.

Alternate Method:

A + B + C → fill tank in 6 hours
They work together for 2 hours, then C is closed
A + B fill remaining tank in 7 hours
We need to find C alone time.
Take LCM of 6 and 7 = 42 units (assume total tank capacity = 42 units)
Work done per hour 
(A + B + C) = 42 ÷ 6 = 7 units/hour
In 2 hours → 7 × 2 = 14 units filled
Remaining = 42 − 14 = 28 units
A + B fill the remaining 28 units in 7 hours →
(A + B) = 28 ÷ 7 = 4 units/hour
Now, C’s 1-hour work = (A + B + C) − (A + B)
= 7 − 4 = 3 units/hour
If C fills 3 units/hour and total = 42 units,
then time = 42 ÷ 3 = 14 hours
Final Answer:
Pipe C alone can fill the tank in 14 hours.

questions.question: There is a water tank of capacity 1500 litres. Two pipes A and B connected with it can fill the tank in 125 hours and 100 hours respectively. The rate at which B fills the tank is what percentage more/less than that of A?
questions.explanation:
Total capacity of the tank = 1500 litres
P = 1500/125 = 12 litres per hour
Q = 1500/100 = 15 litres per hour
Required % = [(15 – 12)/12] * 100 = 25 % more

questions.question: When two inlet pipes, A and B, work together, they can fill a tank in 48 minutes. However, when a leak develops in the tank, it takes an additional 12 minutes to fill. What is the duration taken by the leak alone to empty the tank?
questions.explanation:
Let the capacity of the tank be 240 units (LCM of 48 and 60).

Now, efficiency of both pipes without leakage =\(\frac{240}{48}\) = 5 units/min

And, efficiency of two pipes with leakage = \(\frac{240}{60}\) = 4 units/min

Hence, efficiency of leakage = 5 – 4 = 1 unit/min

Required time taken = \(\frac{240}{1}\)= 240 min = 4 hrs

∴ Time taken by leak alone to empty the tank is 4 hours.

questions.question: Two pipes can fill a cistern separately in 15 hours and 30 hours. They can together fill the cistern in:
questions.explanation:
Let time taken to fill the cistern together be x.

\(= > \frac{1}{15} + \frac{1}{30} = \frac{1}{x}\)

\(= > \ \frac{2}{30} + \frac{1}{30} = \frac{1}{x}\)

\(= > \frac{3}{30} = \frac{1}{x}\)

\(= > x = \ 10\ hours\)

Short Trick:

Pipe A = 15 hours
Pipe B = 30 hours
Take LCM of 15 and 30 = 30 units (assume total work = 30 units)
Work done per hour
A = 30 ÷ 15 = 2 units/hour
B = 30 ÷ 30 = 1 unit/hour
Together they fill = 2 + 1 = 3 units/hour
Total work = 30 units
So, time = 30 ÷ 3 = 10 hours
Final Answer:
The cistern will be filled in 10 hours.

questions.question: Pipe A is 4 times more efficient than B. Pipe A fills the tank in 18 minutes. Find how many minutes the tank will fill when both the pipe is opened?
questions.explanation:
Let the rate at which B fills the tank be 1 l/ min.

So, rate of A\(\  = \ 5l/\ min\)

Total quantity of tank \(= \ 5 \times 18\  = \ 90\ l\)

TIme taken by both to fill the tank\(\  = \ \frac{90}{1 + 5} = \frac{90}{6} = 15\ hrs\)

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 minutes whereas pipe A along with pipe B can fill the same tank in 8 minutes. In what time pipe B alone can fill the tank?
questions.explanation:
Apply formula \(= \frac{\text{XY}}{Y + X}\)

X= 12 minutes

Y=?

As per question;

\(\frac{12 \times Y}{Y + 12} = 8\)

12Y= 8Y+96

4Y= 96

Y = 24 minutes

Alternate Method:

Pipe A fills the tank in 12 minutes.
Pipe A + Pipe B together, fill it in 8 minutes.
Take LCM of 12 and 8 = 24 units (assume total tank capacity = 24 units).
Work done per minute 
A = 24 ÷ 12 = 2 units/min
A + B = 24 ÷ 8 = 3 units/min
Work done by B = (A + B) − A = 3 − 2 = 1 unit/min
So, time taken by B alone = total work ÷ B’s rate
= 24 ÷ 1 = 24 minutes
Final Answer:
Pipe B alone can fill the tank in 24 minutes.

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 20 minutes but due to a leak develop at the bottom of the tank, 1/5 of the water filled by the pipe leaks out. Find the time in which the tank is filled.
questions.explanation:
Let the capacity of the tank be x liters.

The pipe can fill the tank in 20 minutes, which means it can fill(\(\frac{x}{20}\)) liters of water in 1 minute.

However, due to the leak at the bottom of the tank, 1/5 of the water filled by the pipe leaks out. So,

amount of water that remains in the tank after 1 minute\(\  = (\frac{4}{5})\  \times \ (\frac{x}{20})\  = \ \frac{x}{25}\)

effective rate of filling the tank = x25 Liters per minute

Let the tank gets filled in t minutes.

Since the tank gets completely filled, so;

\((\frac{x}{25})\  \times \ t\  = x\)

\(t\  = \ 25\)

Therefore, the tank is filled in 25 minutes.

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 10 mins and the another pipe can empty it in 6 mins. A water tank is two fifths full. If both the pipes are open, how long will it take to empty or fill the tank completely?
questions.explanation:
Given Information:

  • Pipe A can fill the tank in 10 mins 
  • Pipe B can empty the tank in 6 mins
  • Tank initially 2/5 full
  • Both pipes are open, find time to empty or fill the tank completely

Calculation:

Let the capacity of tank be 30 units.
Efficiency of filling pipe \(=\frac{30}{10}=3\) units \(/ min\).
Combined draining efficiency of two pipes \(=-\frac{30}{6}\) \(=-5\) units \(/ min\).
Time required to empty the \(\operatorname{tank}=\frac{30}{5}=6 min\).

 

Concept Used:

When filling and emptying happen simultaneously, net rate = filling rate − emptying rate

Time = Remaining work ÷ Net rate

questions.question: A cistern can be filled with water by pipe A in 8 hours and it can be emptied by a second pipe B in 5 hours. If both the pipes are opened when the cistern is full, the time in which it will be emptied is:
questions.explanation:
Let time taken to empty the tank be x.

Now;

\(\frac{1}{B} - \frac{1}{A} = \frac{1}{x}\)

\( \ \frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{8}\  = \frac{1}{x}\)

\( \frac{8}{40} - \frac{5}{40} = \frac{1}{x}\)

\( \ \frac{1}{x}\  = \ \frac{3}{40}\)

\( \ x\  = \ \frac{40}{3} = 13(\ \frac{1}{3})\)

questions.question: Three pipes P, Q and R can fill a tank in 24 hours. After working together for 8 hours, R is closed and P and Q can fill the remaining part in 20 hours. How much time taken by R to fill the tank alone?
questions.explanation:
Calculations:

The tank will be filled by P, Q, R in 8 hours = 8/24
= 1/3
Remaining work = 1 - 1/3 = 2/3
Time taken by P and Q to fill the tank = 20/2 * 3 =
30 hours
R’s 1 hour work = 1/24 – 1/30 = 1/120
Time taken by R to fill the tank = 120 hours

Alternate Solution:

P, Q, and R together fill the tank in 24 hours
They work together for 8 hours, then R is closed
Remaining part is filled by P and Q in 20 hours
We need to find: Time taken by R alone to fill the tank
Let total work = LCM = 120 units
Work done per hour by all three together:
= 120 ÷ 24 = 5 units/hour
In first 8 hours (all three working),
= 5 × 8 = 40 units completed
So, remaining work = 120 − 40 = 80 units
Remaining 80 units done by P + Q in 20 hours
→ Work rate of (P + Q) = 80 ÷ 20 = 4 units/hour
We know
P + Q + R = 5 units/hour
P + Q = 4 units/hour
⇒ R = 5 − 4 = 1 unit/hour
If R alone does 1 unit per hour and total work is 120 units,
then R alone will take
= 120 ÷ 1 = 120 hours
Final Answer:
R alone can fill the tank in 120 hours.

questions.question: A tank has a leak which can empty a full tank in 28 minutes. A tap is turned on which can fill 2.5 liters a minutes. The tank now becomes empty in 42 minutes. What is the capacity of the tank?
questions.explanation:
Let the capacity of the tank is "C" liters.

According to the problem,

leak can empty the full tank in 28 minutes. This means

rate of the leak , L \(= \ \frac{C}{28} - - - (1)\)

When the tap is turned on, it fills the tank at a rate of 2.5 liters per minute. This means that the effective rate of emptying the tank is reduced by 2.5 liters per minute. Therefore;

new rate of emptying the tank \(= L\  - \ 2.5\  = \ \frac{C}{42} - - - (2)\)

From (1) and (2);

\(\frac{C}{28} - \ 2.5\  = \ \frac{C}{42}\)

\(= > C\  = \ 210\ l\)

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 20 hours while pipe B can fill a tank 30 hours. They were used to fill a empty tank but when the tank was 50% full pipe A was closed then find the additional time required by B to fill the tank?
questions.explanation:
Pipe A can fill a tank in 20 hours.

Pipe B can fill a tank 30 hours.

Total unit of work (L.C.M of 20 and 30) = 60 units

Unit of work done by A in 1 hour = 3

Unit of work done by B in 1 hour = 2

Time required to fill 50% of the tank = 50100×60=30

\(= \frac{30}{5} = \ 6\) hours

Time required to fill the remaining tank by B alone

= \(\frac{30}{2}\) = 15 hours

Total time taken = 6 + 15 = 21 hours

Standard time required = \(\frac{60}{5}\ \)=12 hours

Additional time taken = 9 hours.
